A.explanation: Area is over-rounded to $0.7$ and $\pm 0.1 \text{ m}^2$ is far too large for fractional uncertainties below $1\%$.

B.explanation: Area $0.704 \text{ m}^2$ with fractional uncertainties added gives absolute uncertainty about $0.006 \text{ m}^2$.

C.explanation: It adds absolute uncertainties $0.001 \text{ m} + 0.01 \text{ m} = 0.011 \text{ m}$, but for a product $A = lw$ fractional uncertainties must be added.

D.explanation: It multiplies $50.3$ by $1.40$ without converting $\text{cm}$ to $\text{m}$, giving $70.4$ instead of $0.704 \text{ m}^2$.

hints: Notice the mixed units: width is $(50.3 \pm 0.1) \text{ cm}$ while length is $(1.40 \pm 0.01) \text{ m}$, so convert width to $0.503 \text{ m}$ before multiplying.
For area $A = \text{length} \times \text{width}$, a product, add the two fractional uncertainties $\Delta l/l + \Delta w/w$ to get the fractional uncertainty in $A$.
Calculate $0.1/50.3 + 0.01/1.40$, multiply that sum by the $0.704 \text{ m}^2$ area, and check which option matches that absolute uncertainty and uses $\text{m}^2$.
walkthrough: Convert width to metres: $w = 50.3 \text{ cm} = 0.503 \text{ m}$ with $\Delta w = 0.1 \text{ cm} = 0.001 \text{ m}$, while $l = 1.40 \text{ m}$ with $\Delta l = 0.01 \text{ m}$.
Calculate the best-estimate area: $A = l \times w = 1.40 \times 0.503 = 0.7042 \text{ m}^2$, so $0.704 \text{ m}^2$ to 3 significant figures.
Write each fractional uncertainty: $\Delta w/w = 0.1/50.3 = 0.00199$ and $\Delta l/l = 0.01/1.40 = 0.00714$.
Add fractional uncertainties for multiplication: $\Delta A/A = 0.00199 + 0.00714 = 0.00913$, about $0.91\%$.
Convert to absolute uncertainty: $\Delta A = 0.00913 \times 0.7042 = 0.0064 \text{ m}^2$, about $\pm 0.006 \text{ m}^2$.
Hence $A = (0.704 \pm 0.006) \text{ m}^2$. This is option B.
